  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 883,
      "endEvent": 885,
      "contextStartEvent": 811,
      "contextEndEvent": 959,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "there’s no way for us to establish it historically, because other explanations are always far more likely.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The universal 'always' could insulate historical rejection from any attestation, but this is a probability argument with reasons, not a substitute affirmation (E864–E878). When challenged, Ehrman requires considering every account and rejects categorical impossibility (E917–E923). Whether his rule excludes contrary evidence regardless of merits remains uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1424,
      "endEvent": 1428,
      "contextStartEvent": 1392,
      "contextEndEvent": 1448,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "If you have no assumption about that at all, it would never occur to you",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Ehrman attributes the Petrine reading to prior assumptions after Douthat offers Peter's prominence and Aramaic details (E1417–E1422). This may dismiss contrary interpretation through presumed bias, but surrounding objections concern eyewitness attribution and ancient literary practice (E1392–E1408, E1431–E1448). The passage does not clearly establish an unrestricted critic-discrediting rule."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1624,
      "endEvent": 1629,
      "contextStartEvent": 1547,
      "contextEndEvent": 1647,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "If there are not errors of geography. Then it’s neutral.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Ehrman expressly excludes correct geography as positive evidence while accepting geographical errors as negative evidence (E1624–E1629). This shields the transmission objection from the narrower counterevidence Douthat identifies (E1578–E1587, E1630–E1640). His murder-location analogy supplies an ordinary argument against proving events from geography, so this remains a protected non-slogan argument."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [

      "startEvent": 1962,
      "endEvent": 1968,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "The question of why God allows suffering is not resolved by God himself suffering, but it is at least addressed.",
      "explanation": "Douthat explicitly distinguishes poetic significance from logical resolution. The emotionally meaningful claim does not purport to defeat the suffering objection or make contrary evidence irrelevant."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 645,

      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "if Jesus didn’t exist, you would think his brother would know that.",
